title: Routing: split Dedicated pool traffic by rollout stage (multi-region aware)
author: Mina Haddad
description: This PR updates the routing layer to support stage-based partition selection for Dedicated pools as part of “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools”. Given a Dedicated pool that is under an active rollout plan (control-plane provides a stage distribution and stage target metadata), the router can now deterministically select a stage for each request and route to the corresponding partition/replica set, while preserving existing Dedicated invariants (capacity isolation, multi-region policy, and streaming/session stickiness). Key behaviors: (1) Stage selection is deterministic per routing key (request_id by default; conversation_id/session_id if present) to avoid thrash across retries and streaming follow-up chunks. (2) Stage distribution is applied at the pool level, then mapped per-region in a way that respects region weights and health; if a region is impaired, the router will re-normalize within the remaining healthy regions while keeping stage allocation semantics intact (the split is preserved as best-effort, but correctness/reliability > exact percentages). (3) For small pools, stages are expressed internally as replica partitions when needed (enforced by existing pool sizing/partitioning rules); the router consumes a normalized “stage target” list that is already validated by control plane, but still applies a final guardrail to avoid routing to a stage target with zero ready replicas. (4) Safety fallback: if stage target is unavailable (no ready endpoints, circuit open, or missing/unknown stage config), route to baseline (stable) partition when allowed, else fail closed with a clear reason in routing debug headers; this aligns with current Dedicated failover policy and upcoming gate evaluation semantics. (5) Adds unit tests covering: distribution determinism, multi-region impairment behavior, empty stage target handling, and stickiness across streaming retries. Feature flag: dedicated_staged_rollouts_routing (off by default). Rollout plans and stage definitions are created by control plane (see ENG-5932 / PR-28437); metrics tagging is in PR-28521. Checklist: - [x] Deterministic stage selection (stable hash) - [x] Multi-region policy preserved - [x] No routing to empty targets - [x] Unit tests + fuzz test for distribution - [x] Flagged + safe fallback path - [x] Added debug headers for oncall triage
commits: routing/dedicated: plumb stage distribution into route context
routing/dedicated: deterministic stage selection (hash on routing key)
routing/multi-region: re-normalize stage allocation on region impairment
routing/safety: avoid routing to empty stage targets; baseline fallback
tests: add unit tests for stage split + multi-region + streaming stickiness
docs: add internal comments + debug header descriptions
conversation: Mina Haddad (author): This is the routing-side piece for Dedicated staged rollouts. Control plane will publish a normalized stage distribution + targets per stage; this PR consumes that and selects a stage deterministically per request/session. Biggest open question I had while implementing was multi-region behavior when a region goes impaired mid-stage; I went with re-normalizing within healthy regions while keeping stage selection stable per routing key as much as possible. Please focus review on the fallback semantics and multi-region logic.

Ravi Menon (review): Stage selection: are we hashing on request_id or something stable across retries? If request_id changes for the same logical request, the client might bounce between stages and confuse gate metrics. Can we prefer a session/conversation key when present?

Mina Haddad (author): Yep. Updated to prefer conversation_id, then session_id, then idempotency_key, and only then request_id. For streaming, we use stream_id/session_id to keep chunks pinned. Added tests for retry behavior.

Vikram Singh (review): Concern about small pools: if stage % maps to <1 replica worth of capacity, control plane will convert to replica partitions, but routing still needs to be defensive. What happens when a stage has 0 ready endpoints due to deploy lag? We should not send traffic there even if the hash selects it.

Mina Haddad (author): Agree. Added StageTargetResolver that checks ready endpoints for the selected stage; if none, it attempts baseline fallback (stable stage) if available. If both are empty, it returns a deterministic failure with reason=NO_READY_STAGE_TARGET and sets x-redwood-route-debug: stage_unavailable.

Jordan Lee (review): Please document determinism: given same routing key + same stage config snapshot we should pick same stage. Also we should be explicit about how we handle missing stage config (e.g., rollout plan exists but stage distribution missing due to cache lag). Policy engine wants predictable semantics here.

Mina Haddad (author): Added comments + a small section in code docstring: stage selection is stable hash modulo cumulative weights; missing stage config triggers baseline route (if configured) else fail closed. Also added an explicit metric counter for missing_stage_config so gate eval can treat it as a signal (telemetry tagging comes in 28521).

Peter Holtz (review): Multi-region: in impairment mode you re-normalize weights. That’s fine, but do we risk concentrating all canary traffic into a single region and saturating it? Can we cap per-region stage traffic if headroom is low?

Mina Haddad (author): Added a guard: if multi-region policy marks region as “degraded” (not fully unhealthy), we reduce its effective weight via existing headroom heuristic (same knob we use for Dedicated spillover). Stage split is applied after region selection, so traffic doesn’t force itself into a single region; it follows region weights first, then stages within that region. Added tests for one-region-down scenario and ensured we keep stage split within remaining regions.

Irene Choi (review): Please ensure we don’t break the existing Dedicated ‘pin to region’ behavior for customers that require data residency. If region pinning is configured, we should not re-normalize across other regions; we should fail within the pinned region if it’s down.

Mina Haddad (author): Good catch. Updated: when policy is “pinned” we do not cross region boundaries. In pinned mode, we only re-normalize stages within the pinned region. If pinned region is unhealthy, we fail with x-redwood-route-debug: pinned_region_unavailable. Added a unit test.
Ravi Menon (review): Can you add debug headers that include selected_stage_id and stage_target? Oncall will need this when chasing 429/queue depth regressions.
Mina Haddad (author): Added x-redwood-dedicated-stage and x-redwood-dedicated-stage-target (only when debug headers are enabled / admin). This should help triage. (Telemetry tags are separate.)

Emily Zhao (review): Tests look good. One nit: StageSelector should treat weights that sum to <1 due to rounding as invalid. Control plane should validate, but routing should fail safe rather than silently skew distribution.
Mina Haddad (author): Implemented strict validation: if total_weight not within epsilon of 1.0, we log + increment a counter and use baseline fallback. Also added a test for malformed config.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved after determinism + missing-config semantics were clarified. Please follow up with a short note in the gate-eval PR referencing these headers/metrics.
Vikram Singh (approval): LGTM. Defensive behavior on empty stage targets is the right call.
Peter Holtz (approval): Looks good; thanks for adding pinned-region behavior.
release_notes: Dedicated routing can now split traffic by rollout stage with deterministic selection and safe fallback behavior.
Multi-region Dedicated pools preserve region policies while applying stage split; pinned-region pools do not fail over cross-region.
Adds routing debug headers for selected stage/target (debug-only).
